camera: Canon EOS 5DS R, UV-Vis-IR multispectral conversion (internal UV/IR filter and sensor OLPF removed, Schott WG280 window; colour filter array and microlenses intact)
source: Crowther, J.M. Understanding colour reproduction in multispectral imaging: measuring camera sensor response in the ultraviolet, visible and infrared. The Imaging Science Journal 2019, 67(5), 268-276. https://doi.org/10.1080/13682199.2019.1638664, Figure 5b. Copy of the paper supplied by the author.
method: Traced programmatically from Figure 5b (raster, 900 px wide at 300 ppi): axes calibrated from the gridlines (0-12000 response, 300-800nm), each channel isolated by its line colour, the legend masked out. Each 20nm data point is read as the vertex of the plotted polyline: a straight line is fitted through four samples inside each segment and the two segments meeting at the point are extrapolated to it, weighted towards the less steep one. Checked by overlaying the points on the figure. The author's repeat measurements agree within 3%; this trace adds roughly 1-2 px (about 20-40 response units, under 0.5% of full scale).
occluded: R at 300nm sits under the other lines and is read as 0 (the graph shows it at zero).
green: Green is the paper's G channel; G2 is drawn on top of it and the two coincide to within a line width.
